# AccurateClock

> AccurateClock is a fast, high-precision online clock that provides synchronized time with millisecond accuracy, global timezone support, and analog and digital clock displays.

## Overview

AccurateClock is a web-based time utility designed to display highly accurate synchronized time.

The application includes:

- High-precision time synchronization
- Millisecond-level time display
- Digital clock
- Analog clock
- Global timezone selection
- GMT offset support
- 12-hour and 24-hour time formats
- Light and dark modes
- Round-trip time (RTT) display
- Clock drift estimation
- Responsive design
- Progressive Web App support

## Main Website

- [AccurateClock](https://accurateclock.pages.dev/)

## Key Features

### High-Precision Time

AccurateClock synchronizes with a remote time service and compensates for network round-trip time to provide a more accurate estimate of the current time.

### Global Timezones

Users can select timezones using GMT offsets ranging from GMT-12 through GMT+14.

### Analog and Digital Displays

AccurateClock provides both a precise digital time display and a continuously updating analog clock.

### Time Formats

Users can switch between:

- 12-hour time
- 24-hour time

### Network Information

The application displays:

- Network round-trip time (RTT)
- Estimated clock drift

### Appearance

AccurateClock supports:

- Light mode
- Dark mode

User preferences are saved locally in the browser.

## Intended Use

AccurateClock is useful for:

- Checking the current time
- Comparing time across GMT offsets
- Monitoring clock synchronization
- Viewing precise time measurements
- Using a fullscreen clock display

## Technology

AccurateClock is a browser-based web application using:

- HTML
- CSS
- JavaScript
- Browser performance APIs
- Internationalization APIs for timezone formatting
- Canvas for the analog clock
- Cloudflare-hosted time synchronization services

## Important Notes

AccurateClock is a time utility and should not be treated as a certified scientific, legal, financial, or official atomic time authority.

Network conditions, device clocks, browser behavior, and server availability can affect synchronization accuracy.
